title: Zinc Regulation in Escherichia coli and Chemical Interactions
summary: This cluster revolves around zinc (Zn) regulation in Escherichia coli, a bacterium, and its interactions with various chemicals. The bacterium has several genes and proteins involved in Zn import and storage, including ZRT1, Zrc1, and Crs5. Chemicals like CYT and FTS, which contain Zn, are used in experiments to measure absorbance and identify Zn peaks. FluoZin-3 binds to Zn28.8, and Zn coordination complexes are part of Zn14.7 and Zn21.2. The low-mass Zn pool perturbs Zn, and Zn is stored in Crs5. The cluster also includes various methods and tools, such as CYT10 and FTS10, which are used to analyze Zn interactions.
